metadata.title: DataSentry: Project Film
metadata.persona: Ethan Gomes (narrated in first person; synthetic Kokoro voice)
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Course assignment (INFO 7375 project film): narrate as yourself, no instructor name, persona, or credit line. No composer cold open, no verdict card, no Your Turn. The house outro card (ClaudeTitleOutro) hard-codes the instructor's handle, so the film closes on a drawn beat (BEND) instead; bookend_check.py is expected to report the missing ClaudeTitleOutro.
metadata.audience: INFO 7375 instructor and TAs; a data engineering hiring manager

beats.narration_text: This is a project film by Ethan Gomes, about Data Sentry, in four parts.

shot.visual_intent: Title card: 'Project Film created by Ethan Gomes'; 'DataSentry' large; a rule with one terracotta dot; the four parts listed below it, numbered 1 to 4.
shot.motion_claim: Title card: 'Project Film created by Ethan Gomes'; 'DataSentry' large; a rule with one terracotta dot; the four parts listed below it, numbered 1 to 4.

beats.narration_text: Part one, the executive summary. Companies set rules to catch bad data, like a taxi fare below zero. Data Sentry tests those rules like a spell-checker: hide mistakes on purpose, count which get caught, and which slip through.

shot.visual_intent: A page of writing; terracotta marks hidden in it on purpose; a magnifier passes over and ticks the ones it finds; one mark is left with no tick ('slipped through').
shot.motion_claim: A page of writing; terracotta marks hidden in it on purpose; a magnifier passes over and ticks the ones it finds; one mark is left with no tick ('slipped through').

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Data Sentry is an AI agent that writes data checks for a table, tests them against bad rows I planted, and revises them, until a person approves the final set.

shot.visual_intent: A checkpoint scanner arch with 'DataSentry · an AI agent' beside it; a table (parcel) slides under the arch; a terracotta dot (a planted bad row) lights on it; a tick and 'a person approves'.
shot.motion_claim: A checkpoint scanner arch with 'DataSentry · an AI agent' beside it; a table (parcel) slides under the arch; a terracotta dot (a planted bad row) lights on it; a tick and 'a person approves'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Why it matters: when checks let bad rows through, wrong numbers reach dashboards and decisions. And as AI writes more checks, someone has to grade them.

shot.visual_intent: A table card with terracotta bad rows; an arrow to a bar-chart dashboard card with a terracotta dot on one bar ('wrong numbers'); then a tick and 'graded'.
shot.motion_claim: A table card with terracotta bad rows; an arrow to a bar-chart dashboard card with a terracotta dot on one bar ('wrong numbers'); then a tick and 'graded'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Part two, what others have done. Pandera, D B T and Great Expectations run rules on tables; Amazon's Dee-queue suggests them. I ran one rule, fare can't be negative, in all three: all caught the negative fares, none caught the trips that end before they start.

shot.visual_intent: Recorded output (typeset) of the 2026-10-25 run: the three tools side by side (all PASS clean, FAIL 25 broken), then the answer key: negative fares 25/25 CAUGHT, drop-off before pick-up 0/25 MISSED; tagged "recorded output · <date>".
shot.motion_claim: Recorded output (typeset) of the 2026-10-25 run: the three tools side by side (all PASS clean, FAIL 25 broken), then the answer key: negative fares 25/25 CAUGHT, drop-off before pick-up 0/25 MISSED; tagged "recorded output · <date>".

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: AI already writes tests: Great Expectations' paid Expect A I suggests data checks, and at Meta, AI-written tests built seventy-five percent of the time and passed fifty-seven; a later tool, steered by planted bugs, had seventy-three percent accepted.

shot.visual_intent: Three cards land in a row, each with one big published number: 'GX Cloud ExpectAI / suggests checks'; 'Meta TestGen-LLM 2024 / 75% built · 57% passed'; 'Meta ACH 2025 / 73% accepted'.
shot.motion_claim: Three cards land in a row, each with one big published number: 'GX Cloud ExpectAI / suggests checks'; 'Meta TestGen-LLM 2024 / 75% built · 57% passed'; 'Meta ACH 2025 / 73% accepted'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Mutation testing has graded code tests with planted bugs since nineteen seventy-eight. But in what I found, nobody does that for AI-written data checks on real tables. That's the gap Data Sentry fills.

shot.visual_intent: A comparison grid (constructed from the sources, labelled so): rows mutation testing (1978), Meta ACH, dbt, GX + ExpectAI, DataSentry; columns "data tables", "planted defects", "AI-written checks"; only DataSentry is yes in all three.
shot.motion_claim: A comparison grid (constructed from the sources, labelled so): rows mutation testing (1978), Meta ACH, dbt, GX + ExpectAI, DataSentry; columns "data tables", "planted defects", "AI-written checks"; only DataSentry is yes in all three.

beats.narration_text: Part three, methods. The data is public: New York City yellow taxi trips from January twenty twenty-five, ten thousand rows.

shot.visual_intent: A flat table card; grey rows fill in; labels 'NYC taxi · Jan 2025' and the real sample size from the first run.
shot.motion_claim: A flat table card; grey rows fill in; labels 'NYC taxi · Jan 2025' and the real sample size from the first run.

beats.narration_text: Step one: a planter script breaks copies of the table five different ways, and locks the answer key away.

shot.visual_intent: Titled 'Step 1': a table card, an arrow to a dark planter block, an arrow to a broken copy with terracotta marks ('5 defect types'), and a locked answer key; labels 'planter', 'answer key'.
shot.motion_claim: Titled 'Step 1': a table card, an arrow to a dark planter block, an arrow to a broken copy with terracotta marks ('5 defect types'), and a locked answer key; labels 'planter', 'answer key'.

beats.narration_text: Step two: Claude sees only the column names and types, and writes pandera checks under a contract. A scorer grades them on the clean copy and every broken copy.

shot.visual_intent: Titled 'Step 2': a workstation (Claude) writes check pages; the checks run over a clean and a broken copy; the scorer binder lands with a tick and a dot; labels 'Claude', 'pandera checks', 'scorer'.
shot.motion_claim: Titled 'Step 2': a workstation (Claude) writes check pages; the checks run over a clean and a broken copy; the scorer binder lands with a tick and a dot; labels 'Claude', 'pandera checks', 'scorer'.

beats.narration_text: Step three: the loop. Only the clean copy's results go back, and Claude revises, up to three rounds, all logged. It's built, and it ran.

shot.visual_intent: Titled 'Step 3 · built and run': three stations on a loop (write, score, 'clean-copy results only') joined by arrows; 'up to 3 rounds, all logged'; a tick and 'ran 2026-11-23'.
shot.motion_claim: Titled 'Step 3 · built and run': three stations on a loop (write, score, 'clean-copy results only') joined by arrows; 'up to 3 rounds, all logged'; a tick and 'ran 2026-11-23'.

beats.narration_text: Its tools are fenced: no built-in tools, an empty folder, no answer keys or held-out data, and every checks file must pass a code policy before it runs. Next: a tool menu, with every call checked.

shot.visual_intent: Claude's workstation inside a dashed fence ('no tools · empty folder'); 'no answer keys · no held-out data' under it; a permission gate labelled 'code policy'; a menu card 'next: tool menu' with four tool names, each checked by code.
shot.motion_claim: Claude's workstation inside a dashed fence ('no tools · empty folder'); 'no answer keys · no held-out data' under it; a permission gate labelled 'code policy'; a menu card 'next: tool menu' with four tool names, each checked by code.

beats.narration_text: And a person stays in charge. Before any checks are kept, I'll see the scorecard, the code and its fingerprint, and approve, refuse, or defer. Nothing is kept without that.

shot.visual_intent: Planned (labelled 'planned'): a review card with three rows ('scorecard', 'code', 'sha256 fingerprint'); three buttons land: 'approve' (tick), 'refuse' (dot), 'defer'; 'nothing kept without approval'.
shot.motion_claim: Planned (labelled 'planned'): a review card with three rows ('scorecard', 'code', 'sha256 fingerprint'); three buttons land: 'approve' (tick), 'refuse' (dot), 'defer'; 'nothing kept without approval'.

beats.narration_text: Do I have what I need? Yes: public data, my laptop, and my existing Claude subscription. No API key, no credits.

shot.visual_intent: A checklist card; four ticks land one by one beside 'data: public (NYC TLC)', 'compute: my laptop', 'Claude: my existing subscription', 'API key, credits: none'.
shot.motion_claim: A checklist card; four ticks land one by one beside 'data: public (NYC TLC)', 'compute: my laptop', 'Claude: my existing subscription', 'API key, credits: none'.

beats.narration_text: Part four, evaluation. I measure defect types caught, false alarms on good trips, and crashing checks, on held-out data never used for tuning: a second planting and a second clean copy.

shot.visual_intent: Four record sheets land in a row, numbered 1 to 4, each labelled with one measure: 'defects caught', 'false alarms', 'crashes', 'held-out data'.
shot.motion_claim: Four record sheets land in a row, numbered 1 to 4, each labelled with one measure: 'defects caught', 'false alarms', 'crashes', 'held-out data'.

beats.narration_text: It passes only with all five defect types caught, zero good trips flagged, and no crashing checks, on both plantings. Anything less fails.

shot.visual_intent: The pass line as a card titled 'pass line': three conditions, each with a tick ('5 of 5 defect types caught', '0 good trips flagged', '0 crashing checks'), then 'on both plantings · anything less fails'.
shot.motion_claim: The pass line as a card titled 'pass line': three conditions, each with a tick ('5 of 5 defect types caught', '0 good trips flagged', '0 crashing checks'), then 'on both plantings · anything less fails'.

beats.narration_text: By hand, nothing passed. In the loop, round one flagged ninety-four good trips, round two just one, and round three none, with all five caught: pass line met. On the second clean copy, still zero.

shot.visual_intent: Recorded output (typeset) of the live loop run (./run_loop.sh, 2026-11-23): round 1, 94 good rows flagged, 5 of 5 (dot); round 2, 1 flagged, 5 of 5 (dot); round 3, PASS, 5 of 5 on both plantings (tick); second clean copy, 0 flagged (tick); tagged "Claude Opus 5.5 · recorded output · <date>".

beats.narration_text: I'll also break it on purpose, at least five ways, like a forbidden import or a try at the answer key. And one controlled failure: I'll trigger the rule-dropping Claude did by hand; the held-out scorer must catch it, and I'll refuse it at the gate.

shot.visual_intent: Planned (labelled 'planned'): five small labels land, each with a terracotta dot ('forbidden import', 'crashing check', 'hard-coded values', 'empty reply', 'answer-key read'); then a row 'controlled failure: predict → trigger → caught by held-out → refused at the gate'.
shot.motion_claim: Planned (labelled 'planned'): five small labels land, each with a terracotta dot ('forbidden import', 'crashing check', 'hard-coded values', 'empty reply', 'answer-key read'); then a row 'controlled failure: predict → trigger → caught by held-out → refused at the gate'.
